problems.title: Global level comparison omits the quadratic shift cost

problems.proved_evidence: Integer times0,...,4 yield5 iid standard normals; theta^delta(4)>=-5/4 logQ(delta)~5delta²/8, theta^-delta(4)->0. Fixed Cdelta cannot dominate. Correct shifted likelihood q/p=exp(-ax-a²/2).

Small delta comparison is repaired by Cdelta+C'delta²+log2/T; limiting local continuity is not refuted.

Integer values 0,...,4 are five iid N(0,1), yielding theta^delta(4)>=-5logQ(delta)/4~5delta^2/8, whereas continuous bounded paths give theta^-delta(4)->0. independent_verification.assessment: For rho=delta0 the printed RHS is zero but E sup|f|=sqrt(2/pi); radius .1 has fixed probability below 1/2 regardless of interval length. For any nonzero variance, shrinking the interval cannot remove the absolute base value. Independently checked anchored metric entropy: log moment gives E sup|f(t)-f(0)|<=C(log1/h)^(-beta/2). Symmetric convex base-value and increment events obey Gaussian correlation; variance<=2B yields q=(1/2)P(|N(0,2B)|<ell/2)>0. Repeated correlation gives q^ceil(T/h)>=exp(-CT) for T>=1.
independent_verification.counterevidence: This restores the ell>0 conclusion of Lemma2.22; fractional-power small-mass Lemma2.20 can absorb the retained base standard deviation using bounded total mass. Original operative chain into Lemma2.23 still invalid as printed; Major does not mean false final small-ball theorem.

problems.title: Spectral projection fails for an origin atom
problems.proved_evidence: C1=(1+cos t)/2,S1=sin t/2,coefficient mass1. At0 variance saturates and independent residual R0=0; atpi coefficients vanish. Predicted covariance0 contradicts actual-1/3.
counterevidence_and_alternative_readings: Both denominators nonzero; not an empty-bin convention.
Separate zero atom and reflected positive-negative bins repairs Hilbert projection; rank-one cost does not alter singular ball exponent.
Counterexample not claimed to satisfy extra Prop5.3 mass constraints.
problems.repair_status: Origin atom separation and rank-one impact justified; no false final theorem established.

independent_verification.assessment: For (delta_-1+delta0+delta1)/3 with D=n1, exact bins give C=(1+cos t)/2,S=sin t/2,total coefficient mass1. At0 variance is exhausted by zeta, so independent residual R0=0. Atpi both displayed coefficients vanish; asserted decomposition predicts covariance0, whereas actual covariance is-1/3. Both bin denominators nonzero. Source p27 explicitly invokes this decomposition for singular spectra.
independent_verification.repair: Separate the origin atom as an independent constant Gaussian, then use symmetric strictly-positive/negative bins. This rank-one addition has fixed positive ball probability and does not change zero exponential rate. Main theorem not disproved; extra Prop5.3 mass conditions not claimed for this counterexample.

problems.title: Rapidly oscillating density does not have the claimed averaged limits
problems.proved_evidence: I(x)=integral0x cos(1/t)dt=-x²sin(1/x)+2integral_(1/x)^infinity sin(u)/u³du, |I|<=2x². Averaged density converges(a+b)/2, neither liminf a nor limsup b; necessary <=3a/2 subsequence absent for a<b/3.
counterevidence_and_alternative_readings: Pointwise oscillation is not averaged oscillation.
Theorem1 would yield existence for this same density, but its proof is not used as an independent proof of the final exponent.
Slow cos(loglog(e/|λ|)) provides different density with oscillating averages; persistence bounds need actual cited hypotheses.
problems.core_dependency: Advertised sharpness/nonexistence example Remark1 and§5.4; its core derivation(5.19) fails.
problems.repair_status: Direct analytic disproof complete; alternative averaged-density construction proved, probability estimates/normalization and reference-version comparison not certified.

independent_verification.assessment: Direct substitution u=1/t and integration by parts gives I(x)=-x^2 sin(1/x)+2integral_(1/x)^infinity sin(u)/u^3, |I|<=2x^2. Hence averaged density ->(a+b)/2. For a<b/3 the required <=3a/2 subsequence on p42 is absent. This invalidates an advertised core nonexistence illustration, independently of any disputed main theorem proof.
independent_verification.counterevidence: Theorem1 and the displayed example cannot both hold, but no independent assertion of the final exponent is derived from the contested theorem. Checked replacement slow phase: log(1+log(1/u)/log(e/x))<=log(1/u)/log(e/x), integrable in u, so averaged and endpoint cos differ by O(1/log(e/x)). This proves only new averaged oscillations; persistence comparison and cited journal-version hypotheses remain unverified as disclosed.

problems.proved_evidence: For MA, all N+2 Gaussians in(-.5,.5) imply persistence at-1, so limsup theta<=-.log P(|Z|<.5)=.95991634. Constant atom has theta0 for every level. For Z+g, union Borell gives P(sup|g|<=A0+sqrt(2log4ceilT))>=1/2; Gaussian tail lower persistence=e^-O(logT), hence theta0 despite nonzero ac.

independent_verification.assessment: For U0=1,U1=-1 the N+2 underlying normals in(-.5,.5) imply Xj>-1, giving finite limsup rate -logP(|Z|<.5), contradicting Example3's all-real-level infinite-rate claim. For rho=delta0, persistence is Q(ell) and rate0. For Z+g with unit-variance bandlimited g, union Borell over ceilT intervals gives probability >=1/2 that sup|g|<=A0+sqrt(2log(4ceilT)); independent common Z then gives lower persistence .5Q(ell+R_T)=exp(-O(logT)), so rate0 despite nonzero ac component.

Restoring ell>=0 in the zero-density application and finite positive origin density in Remark3 avoids the examples.
